<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 10321fa22d5dd75a25dfd779b077aa94a563e3e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fe6a23a1415f2d728f3666daea5253d8b6be0d73` — the merge of head `c2c17a47a2b90095f5780cdd6ee31b3312449563` into base `10321fa22d5dd75a25dfd779b077aa94a563e3e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fe6a23a1415f2d728f3666daea5253d8b6be0d73 && git checkout fe6a23a1415f2d728f3666daea5253d8b6be0d73
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 10321fa22d5dd75a25dfd779b077aa94a563e3e2 c2c17a47a2b90095f5780cdd6ee31b3312449563 && git checkout -B drift-repro 10321fa22d5dd75a25dfd779b077aa94a563e3e2 && git merge --no-ff c2c17a47a2b90095f5780cdd6ee31b3312449563

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 10321fa22d5dd75a25dfd779b077aa94a563e3e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 10321fa22d5dd75a25dfd779b077aa94a563e3e2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2c17a47a2b90095f5780cdd6ee31b3312449563`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-security-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #38131 for card #37535, read against the ruled terms (i) to (v) and the premise clause copied into the card body from ruling record 7190344023. Read-only: the card and its four comments, the PR body, file list and net diff against `main`, the check-runs on this head, and the cited code in the head tree. `Security-touching: yes` because the hunks change permission behaviour: a predicate update or delete now writes rows an app-authored policy admits. No path under `.claude/**` is touched, so no hunk changes a rule.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, spec**: one optional member on `ISecurityService`, `getAuthoredRowWriteFilter?(object, operation, context)`, returning `Promise` of `FilterCondition | undefined`. Right: it is the ruling's "optional filter-shaped answer ... for an object, a verb and a caller". It reuses `AuthoredRowWriteOperation` and `FilterCondition`, adds no type and no Zod schema, and an implementation that predates it still satisfies the contract.
- **Accept-set, behaviour**: a predicate (`multi: true`) update or delete under record sharing now reaches the rows an authored `using` policy for that verb admits. This is a widening, and it is the one the ruling ordered (term (i)). Right. Nothing accepted before is refused after, so no narrowing arm is owed.
- **Accept-set, unchanged cases**: a caller with no authored `using` policy, a check-only policy, a delegated write, a sharing scope that is already `null`, a security service without the member, and any failure all keep the scope `main` has. Right, by terms (iii) and (iv).
- **Registered service**: `registered-security-service-members.pin.test.ts` lists the member as `optional`, and the registration in `security-plugin-security-service.ts` serves it. Right.
- **plugin-sharing surface**: `SharingSecurityProbe` gains the optional structural member and `SharingService` gains the public method `probeAuthoredRowWriteFilter`. `ISharingService` in the spec is not touched. Right: the composition is the middleware's own, as the ruling says.
- **Gate verdicts on this head**: 42 check-runs concluded `success` and 10 `skipped`, none failed. That includes Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Build Core and the Dogfood Regression Gate. **15 runs had not concluded when this record was rendered**: Test Core shards 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 of 10, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI, and eight Test UI shards. Those Test Core shards and the workspace type check are the runs that carry the moved pins, so this record gives no gate verdict for them. It judges the contract and the design; the queue's required checks still have to conclude green on this head.

### ② Semver level

Three changesets, one per moved package (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`), each `patch`, each carrying both declaration lines.

- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. Nothing a metadata author can write changes: no key, value or metadata type is added, removed or re-read. By the AGENTS.md rule the level follows that kind alone, so `none` takes `patch` on all three, including the additive contract member and the behaviour change.
- No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker are owed: nothing is removed, renamed or refused.

Clause-②: yes — right. The diff changes a published contract (`ISecurityService`) and published write behaviour. The bare `yes` is well formed; a `(widening)` arm would also have been true and is optional. The PR body and all three changesets carry the same line.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question 1, the third pin** (`plugin-security/src/operator-id-write-gate-33928.test.ts`): answered **A, accepted as within the ruling**. Term (v) names two pins, but it lists them as what moves, not as a limit on what may move. The governing words are term (i), "Bulk scope = sharing scope OR authored scope", and the named premise, "the rows a predicate write changes equal the rows the by-id write admits". The old expectation in this file was the negation of that sentence on one row: the two-key `{ id, stage }` predicate "leaves the row" while the by-id write of the same row writes it. It cannot stay green under the ruled behaviour, and its new expectation is the premise itself (the predicate writes the row, as by id). No product choice moved. I checked the dev's claim that the file's other purpose survives: plugin-sharing's file of the same name still pins which branch each option shape takes (`admitsByIdWrite` against `buildWriteFilter`, over the engine's dispatch table). Nothing here needs the maintainer.

**Open question 2, the member name** `getAuthoredRowWriteFilter`: answered **A, keep**. The ruling names no member. Its words are "an optional filter-shaped answer: the authored policies' own scope for an object, a verb and a caller, with the platform ownership floor taken out". The signature `(object, operation, context)` is that object, verb and caller, and the name follows the two precedents on the same contract: `getReadFilter` for a filter that answers `undefined`, and `checkAuthoredRowWrite` for the same question as a verdict. One caution, which the jsdoc already covers: `getReadFilter` narrows and this member may only widen, and the jsdoc says so with its own ⛔ and in the contract header's failure-class list. No escalation.

**Dev deviations**: the extra files (`security-plugin-security-service.ts`, the members pin, the two middleware doubles, the dogfood probe, `rls.mdx`) are each forced by the change or by term (v). `security-plugin-security-service.ts` is where the registration lives, so it is in my scope and is judged in ④. The tests, the dogfood probe, the changesets' prose and `content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx` are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. One note for that seat: the moved plugin-security test's header still opens "The declared narrowing of the sharing write gate", above a body that now pins the opposite.

**SQL push-down**: no finding. The new answer is a compiled predicate ORed into the write's `where`; the diff adds no id materialisation, no in-app join and no read. The ruling's "does not probe row by row on the bulk path" holds: the bulk branch makes one call per write and `getAuthoredRowWriteFilter` reads nothing.

**Ruled prohibitions**: `buildWriteFilter`, `checkEdit` and `checkDelete` are not in the diff's hunks. The 2026-08-15 no-marking block above the bulk branch is intact and the new composition is unmarked, as that block requires.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`** (hit), read against the ruling and its first consumer, the sharing middleware's bulk branch:

- "a row matches the filter iff `checkAuthoredRowWrite` answers `admit` for it": holds by construction. Both read one helper, `authoredRowWriteLayers`; the verdict probes `{ id } AND layer0 AND layer1` and the filter is `layer0 AND layer1`. A pin compares the two row for row on both verbs.
- "with the platform's ownership floor taken out" and the tenant wall kept: holds. The floor leaves through the sets by provenance, and Layer 0 is ANDed beside Layer 1.
- "`undefined` is the fail-closed answer", with its five listed cases: each maps to a `null` from the helper or to the `catch`. The superuser case rests on `computeLayeredRlsFilter` answering a null Layer 1, which the verdict's existing docblock states and which this diff does not change.
- "Verb for verb" and "a caller maps lifecycle verbs onto these two classes itself": the middleware passes `rlsOperationForVerb(op)`.
- "Evidence, not authorization" and "only to WIDEN ... by OR, never to narrow": the one consumer ORs it, and plugin-security's own layers still run on the write.
- "OPTIONAL ... callers feature-detect": the consumer checks `typeof probe.getAuthoredRowWriteFilter !== 'function'`.

**Trying to break it.** The ruling's premise is predicate rows = by-id rows. At the sharing gate the two are the same expression: by id, `admitsByIdWrite` is the per-verb gate OR the verdict; in bulk, the scope is `buildWriteFilter` OR the filter.

- *A `private` object, cross-owner row, no read grant.* By id the row is refused by plugin-security's pre-image read. If the bulk path lacked that read bound, the new OR would write rows by predicate that by id refuses. It does not: plugin-security ANDs `readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite` into every addressed predicate write, so the row is not matched. The two paths agree.
- *Delegated write.* By id, both identities are gated and the verdict abstains. In bulk, the middleware guard, the passthrough and the helper each abstain on `onBehalfOf`, and the delegator intersection is composed before the OR and never widened. Three guards for one rule is redundant but safe, and ablation B shows the controls go red without them.
- *Order of composition.* The OR sits after the delegator AND and before `composeAnd(ast.where, ...)`, so the caller's own predicate still bounds the write and the authored scope cannot escape it.
- *A sharing scope that denies everything.* It is non-null, so the authored scope is ORed in. By id the same caller is admitted by the verdict alone, so this is equal, not wider.
- *A `null` sharing scope.* Not asked, and correct: nothing narrows there, so there is nothing to widen.
- *A hostile or broken answer.* The passthrough accepts only a non-array object and logs a throw once. An empty object would match every row, but only if plugin-security itself compiled an authored Layer 1 to that, in which case the verdict admits every row by id too.

**Implementing files, against the contract:**

- `security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts`: the moved head is the old body line for line, with `return 'abstain'` turned into `return null`. `checkAuthoredRowWrite` keeps its guards in the same order, then the helper, then the same elevated id-only probe. The by-id verdict does not change.
- `security-plugin.ts` and `security-plugin-security-service.ts`: the method and the registration follow the existing host-literal shape, and the docblock agrees with the spec jsdoc.
- `sharing-service.ts`: `probeAuthoredRowWriteFilter` mirrors `probeAuthoredRowWrite` guard for guard, and feeds none of `buildWriteFilter`, `checkEdit` or `checkDelete`.
- `sharing-plugin.ts`: the hunk is terms (i) to (iv) and nothing more.

**Nits** (no effect on correctness or the contract; a fix would move the head, so each is left as an accepted deviation):

- N1 (nit) — the module header of `security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts` still describes a module that holds the verdict alone, "moved ... otherwise unedited". It now also holds `authoredRowWriteLayers` and the exported `getAuthoredRowWriteFilter`.
- N2 (nit) — both `catch` blocks call `this.logger.warn?.(...)`, which would itself throw if `logger` were unset, against "never throws outward". This is the verdict's existing pattern, and the service is registered only after `start()` assigns the logger.

Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSAaBEfQpU2yJexSJ8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

4. **L2** — the owed `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review (face: published schema `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`) is **PASS on this head**, record 7233479562 (isolated at-tier subagent; no must-fix, no should-fix; nits N1, N2 accepted). It answered the dev's two open questions as A within the ruling: the third moved pin (`operator-id-write-gate-33928.test.ts`) is the negation of the ruling's premise on one row; the member name follows `getReadFilter` / `checkAuthoredRowWrite` on the same contract.

The `Known limitation` callout below it still holds: the read bound stays ANDed on every predicate write (L2 ④).
